title: You Need a New CFO | Andreessen Horowitz
gist: a16z partner Seema Amble argues AI-native tools have removed data as the finance bottleneck, turning the CFO from scorekeeper into builder of the company's operating system. Finance teams shrink (leanest target ~2% of headcount vs ~5%), a 'finance engineer' role emerges (e.g. Anthropic's 70+ finance AI skills), planning goes continuous, and finance gains a mandate over compute, pricing and people-vs-software decisions.

themes.theme: CFO archetype shift: accountant to banker to builder

insights.claim: Each era hires the CFO archetype matching its scarce skill: Big 4 accountants for books and controls, investment bankers for capital raising, FP&A/PE profiles for planning and metrics; today's scarce skill is designing the company's operating system (data, workflows, agents, skills, controls).
insights.speaker: Seema Amble
insights.so_what: Hiring signals for finance leadership shift toward technical builders; a talent-market tailwind for AI-native finance tooling vendors.
insights.quote: Today’s scarce skill is something new: designing the operating system the company runs on.
insights.locator: From accountant to banker to builder

insights.claim: Leading finance teams aim for a zero-day close and continuously updated forecasts, replacing the monthly close rhythm; OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar frames finance as a real-time function.
insights.speaker: Seema Amble
insights.so_what: Monthly-cadence finance software and processes face obsolescence pressure.
insights.quote: Finance is building toward a zero-day close and a continuously updated forecast
insights.locator: The finance leaders operating this way

insights.claim: The AI-native CFO must be automation-first and needs new frameworks for build vs. buy and ROI of automation, with the payoff being more time as strategic partner to the CEO.
insights.speaker: Seema Amble
insights.so_what: CFO competency models and evaluation criteria for finance leaders will be rewritten around automation design.
insights.quote: The AI-native CFO has to be automation-first
insights.locator: The CFO is becoming a builder

themes.theme: AI-native finance stack does the work

insights.claim: AI has removed data as the CFO's bottleneck: extracting and interpreting data scattered across systems, spreadsheets, email and Slack is now fast, shifting finance time from acquiring information to acting on it.
insights.speaker: Seema Amble
insights.so_what: Value in finance software migrates from data plumbing to decisioning and automated execution.
insights.locator: 1. Data stopped being the bottleneck.

insights.claim: A new generation of finance software stands up in days rather than quarters, collects data automatically and delivers real-time insight; every layer of a16z's 2020 finance-stack market map now has an AI-native contender, from ERP to tax to procurement.
insights.speaker: Seema Amble
insights.so_what: Incumbent finance suites (ERP, tax, procurement, AR) face AI-native challengers across every category simultaneously.

insights.so_what: Addressable market expands from software budgets into labor and outsourced services spend (e.g. audit, tax, AR).

insights.claim: A 'finance engineer' role is emerging: finance people, often with engineering background, proficient in Codex or Claude Code, who build internal tools, automations and dashboards; the author says this was not predicted in their 2020 piece.
insights.speaker: Seema Amble
insights.so_what: Parallels GTM/growth engineer trend; demand for coding-agent tools spreads into back-office functions.

insights.claim: The old heuristic of finance at ~5% of company headcount is breaking; the leanest teams target ~2%, prioritizing talent density.
insights.speaker: Seema Amble
insights.so_what: Implies up to ~60% reduction in finance headcount per company at the frontier; pressure on finance/accounting labor and outsourced services.
insights.quote: The leanest teams we see are targeting 2%
insights.locator: 4. The finance team gets smaller

insights.claim: The layered controller/FP&A/ops structure existed to move and reconcile data on a monthly cadence; as that work automates, the structure itself becomes obsolete and AI fluency (APIs, SQL, prototyping) becomes a baseline hiring requirement.
insights.speaker: Seema Amble
insights.so_what: Finance hiring profiles and org design shift; implications for accounting-education pipelines.
insights.quote: “Walk me through your model” is becoming “walk me through your prompt sequence.”
insights.locator: Most finance teams are still organized

insights.claim: Usage-based revenue (tokens, minutes, API calls) and agents acting in the P&L make monthly planning too slow; FP&A is moving from annual budgeting to continuous forecasting using statistical models, account-level evidence and judgment, with scenarios run live in meetings.
insights.speaker: Seema Amble
insights.so_what: Demand for real-time planning tools grows with consumption-priced AI businesses.
insights.quote: FP&A is evolving from annual budgeting to continuous operating decisions.
insights.locator: 5. Planning becomes continuous.

insights.claim: As software does more finance work, an auditable chain from every number to its source, including which agents were involved, becomes a core product feature; agents drafting journal entries must keep evidence and follow approval rules, with finance owning sign-off.
insights.speaker: Seema Amble
insights.so_what: Auditability/provenance is a competitive moat for AI finance vendors and a gating factor for adoption.
insights.locator: 6. Controls become a critical feature

themes.theme: Finance's expanding mandate: compute, pricing, people vs. software

insights.claim: For many AI companies compute is among the largest opex items and most consequential capital allocation decisions, pulling finance into pricing, product launches and spending commitments by modeling usage, infrastructure costs and revenue together.
insights.speaker: Seema Amble
insights.so_what: CFOs become central to compute procurement and AI gross-margin management.
insights.quote: compute is one of the biggest operating expenses and most consequential capital allocation decisions
insights.locator: 7. Finance gets a bigger mandate.

insights.claim: Dividing work between people and software is becoming a finance decision, using granular data on time, token usage and software utilization; build vs. buy now spans vibecoded internal tools to outcome/usage-priced purchases whose costs scale with adoption.
insights.speaker: Seema Amble
insights.so_what: Labor-vs-software allocation becomes a CFO-owned budgeting line; outcome-based pricing complicates spend forecasting.
insights.quote: how teams divide work between people and software is a key question across organizations and is a finance decision

insights.claim: Example finance-engineer tool: combine customer revenue with model inference, cloud and support costs to flag accounts whose margins deteriorate or contracts become unprofitable due to usage.
insights.speaker: Seema Amble
insights.so_what: Per-account margin monitoring is a key need for AI businesses with variable inference costs.
